target.title: Fix stranded menu scroll after a manual refresh clears a provider error
target.body:
Fixes #2046.

## Problem

When a provider error (red multi-line banner in the top card) is present and the user clicks the persistent **Refresh** row, the refresh updates the open menu's cards in place — but a taller-than-screen tracked menu is left anchored mid-scroll: the viewport never returns to the top, and closing + reopening the menu is the only recovery.

## Fix (rev 3 — addresses both ClawSweeper findings)

Run a **viewport restore directly from the manual-refresh completion path**, bound to **the menu that initiated the refresh**: `refreshMenuProviderNow` captures the initiating menu's identity when the refresh starts, and completion restores only that same menu if it is still open, non-hosted, and dirty — one main-actor turn later so the unfrozen card layout settles.

- **Rev 2** (P1): the first revision armed a pending intent consumed only by an open-menu rebuild, but explicit store actions intentionally defer visible parent rebuilds while the menu is tracking — so the intent never fired on the reported flow and could linger for an unrelated later rebuild. The restore now executes from `startManualRefresh`'s completion with no pending state and no interaction with the rebuild path.
- **Rev 3** (P2): completion no longer scans all open dirty menus. Shared refresh invalidation dirties every open root menu, so a menu opened and scrolled while another menu's refresh was in flight could have been yanked to the top. The restore is keyed to the initiating menu ID captured at start; the menu-switch scenario has a dedicated regression test.

Background data ticks never take this path, so they can never move a viewport the user is reading.

## How the scroll repair works (probed on macOS 26.2)

Standalone AppKit probes against the view-based menu implementation (tall menu of custom-view rows, mutated and scrolled while tracking) established:

- A tracked menu is `NSPopupMenuWindow` → `NSMenuScrollView` (a real `NSScrollView`) → `NSClipView` → `NSTableViewBackedMenuRepresentation`, plus two arrow `NSImageView` strips.
- Row views are **recycled** once they scroll offscreen (`item.view` detaches; `enclosingScrollView` goes nil), so the shared scroll view is resolved through whichever item view is currently attached (`attachedMenuScrollView(in:)`).
- The offset is read and corrected with public API only: `NSView.enclosingScrollView`, `NSClipView.scroll(to:)`, `NSScrollView.reflectScrolledClipView(_:)`. The repair runs inside `performMenuMutationWithoutAnimation` and no-ops when the menu is not scrolled, not oversized, closed, or has no attached window.
- The flipped/non-flipped top-offset math is a pure helper (`menuViewportTopOffset`) with unit coverage.

## Verification

- `make test` — full suite green.
- `make check` — SwiftFormat + SwiftLint --strict clean.
- `swift test --filter StatusMenuViewportRestoreTests` — 9 tests.
- `swift test --filter StatusMenuOpenRefreshTests` — 31 tests green (the deferral baseline the review cited; this fix no longer interacts with the rebuild path at all).
- **End-to-end state test through the production path**: `manual refresh completion restores the open dirty menu viewport end to end` drives `performPersistentRefreshAction(in:)` (the same entry the persistent Refresh row and ⌘R use) on an open tracked menu and asserts the restore fires after completion **without any parent rebuild landing** (the test also asserts the menu is still dirty afterwards, i.e. the deferral behavior the review cited is preserved and the restore no longer depends on a rebuild).
- **Menu-switch regression test**: `menu opened during another menus in-flight refresh is never restored` starts a gated refresh from menu A, closes A, opens menu B mid-flight, completes the refresh, and asserts B is dirty from shared invalidation yet never restored. Companion negatives: a clean initiating menu is not restored; an initiating menu closed mid-flight gets no restore; background rebuilds never restore.

## Fresh-bundle proof status

I attempted the requested fresh-bundle recording and hit a data-safety wall I don't want to work around dishonestly: this machine is my daily driver with a live CodexBar install, and a debug bundle resolves the real user home for provider detection, local cost logs, and Codex auth — so even under an isolated `$HOME` the "synthetic" instance surfaces my real accounts and usage, and seeding `~/.codexbar/config.json` with synthetic providers would also reconfigure the live install. Producing the recording safely needs a clean macOS user account, which I'll set up if you want the video before merging.

Reproducible recipe (clean user account or sandbox machine): `./Scripts/package_app.sh debug` → launch → Debug pane → Error Simulation → set a multi-line error on Claude → make the menu taller than the screen (several providers or stacked token accounts) → open menu, scroll to the bottom, ⌘R → on this branch the viewport re-anchors at the top with the recovered header visible; on `main` it stays stranded.

No keychain access, no provider I/O, UI-layer only. CHANGELOG left untouched per house practice.

Suggested release-note line, if useful: *Menu: re-anchor the open menu at the top after a manual refresh, so a taller-than-screen menu is never stranded mid-scroll once a provider error banner clears; background refreshes never move the viewport.*

target.title: fix: suspension and restart wait for background execs
target.body:
Fixes #104079

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where hosts using cooperative Gateway suspension or safe restart could receive an idle result while an approved background exec process was still running. A visible process entry could also be removed before the operating-system process had actually exited, leaving the remaining work unaccounted for.

## Why This Change Was Made

The process registry now retains a count-only live background-exec marker through confirmed exit. Detached approval execution atomically hands work from Gateway root admission to that marker, while suspension and every safe-restart path account for both sides of the handoff. The protocol exposes only an aggregate `background-exec` blocker; commands, PIDs, output, and session identifiers remain private.

## User Impact

Hosting controllers no longer freeze, snapshot, or restart the Gateway across a live background command. `process remove` can still hide a session immediately, but lifecycle admission remains blocked until the process owner confirms exit.

Release-note context: cooperative suspension and safe restart now wait for live background exec sessions.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `blue-prawn` / [run 29139283576](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29139283576): 207 focused test executions passed across registry, detached approval, suspension, restart, reload, and protocol suites.
- `pnpm protocol:check` passed.
- `pnpm build` passed.
- `pnpm check:changed -- <touched files>` passed, including core/test typecheck and the full core lint fan-out.
- `pnpm docs:check-mdx`, `pnpm docs:check-links`, `pnpm docs:check-i18n-glossary`, and `pnpm format:docs:check` passed; link audit checked 5,807 internal links with zero broken links.
- Fresh autoreview: clean, no actionable findings.
